Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Clothes & getting dressed

formal adjective

not casual: of dress, language, manner

also informal, formal dress, formal clothes, dress up, a formal letter, formal language, casual (not formal)

classical

Liv. 33.47.10: vestītū forēnsī
Cic. Fin. 2.77: ut vestītum … aliam domesticam, aliam forēnsem

forēnsis, forēnse

adjective, third declension

formal (of dress): worn in public, against what one wears at home

“Of the forum”, public; of clothes, the dress one goes out in, against domesticus, what one wears at home (Lewis & Short). Suetonius calls formal dress simply forēnsia (Aug. 73). Its other common sense is “of the courts”, forensic.

Other words

  • sevērus et gravis — formal, serious (of a letter, of speech)

    phrase: two adjectives · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 2.4.1: ūnum familiāre et jocōsum, alterum sevērum et grave

    Cicero’s two kinds of letter: the familiar and joking, and the serious and weighty. So informal is familiāris, formal gravis.

  • lautus, lauta, lautum — dressy, formal (of clothes)

    also used · modern · M-O s.v. formal (of clothing)

    Classically “washed”, and so neat, elegant, sumptuous, of a fine dinner or a well-off man (Lewis & Short, s.v. lavō); Morgan–Owens applies it to formal clothes and gives cotīdiānus for informal ones.

Examples

  • ut vestītum, sīc sententiam habeās aliam domesticam, aliam forēnsem

    that you should have one opinion for home and another for public, as you do with your clothesCic. Fin. 2.77

  • reliqua sunt epistulārum genera duo, quae mē magnō opere dēlectant, ūnum familiāre et jocōsum, alterum sevērum et grave

    there remain two kinds of letter which give me great pleasure, one familiar and joking, the other serious and formalCic. Fam. 2.4.1

  • prīmīs tenebrīs vestītū forēnsī ad portam cum duōbus comitibus ignārīs cōnsiliī est ēgressus

    as soon as it was dark he went out to the gate, in his ordinary public dress, with two companions who knew nothing of his planLiv. 33.47.10

See also formal, domestic, polite, clothes.
